content_details.name: Kinsoku Ryokan
content_details.short_description: Follow the ever-changing taboos, complete your exorcism missions, and make it back alive. A horror action game featuring the story of Satomi, an apprentice shrine maiden, and online play for up to 8 players.
content_details.about_the_game:
Obey the rules. Finish the mission. Make it out alive.

The spirits are not the only danger waiting inside.

Do not run. Do not close doors. Stop when the bell rings.

Changing rules shape every step you take through a haunted location.

KINSOKU RYOKAN is a horror action game about completing your mission and escaping alive.

Proceed carefully on your own, or divide the work among teammates.

Do not let your guard down when the exit opens.

Changing rules. Unfinished work.

Explore haunted buildings and tackle tasks involving sealing, exorcism, combat and repairs.

Breaking a rule can do more than hurt you: a completed task may reactivate, or corruption may advance.

Read the current restrictions and prepare for the next set before it takes effect.

An ally can join the spirit side

In online play, corruption can turn a player into a spirit working against the humans’ mission.

Spirit form, exposure and human banishment create a struggle that goes beyond cooperation.

The situation changes again when escape becomes available. Keep fighting for your return until the final step.

Satomi’s story—and more ways to play

  • A single-player Story Mode following Satomi Himuro, an apprentice miko.

  • Solo play with selectable stages and settings.

  • Steam online play for up to 8 players, with public rooms, password-protected rooms and Quick Match.

  • Distinct strengths for Miko, Sister, Martial Artist, Agent and Apprentice Miko jobs.

  • Room settings for NPC spirits, rain, vision range, time limits, possession and more.

  • A Heroine & Outfit Gallery for inspecting unlocked models, viewing actions and reading descriptions.

Controls and languages

Play with keyboard and mouse, with partial controller support.

A keyboard is required for names, passwords, chat and some bonus-area actions.

Japanese and English are supported, with an in-game display-language selector.

content_details.name: Mors Blade - UNSLASHED
content_details.short_description: Blades and scarabs locked in a tango of death. A multi-ending sci-fi seinen visual novel inspired by 90s anime OVAs. Will you find the truth behind the alien invasion? Or will you bring the world to the brink of destruction again?
content_details.about_the_game:
From the hand that created Schwarzerblitz and 8-Colors Star Guardians, here comes a new hand-crafted sci-fi visual novel!

God is dead. Long live God

Senna is a Blade, one of the three girls that received the power to turn into hi-tech bioweapons from the mechanical rabbit Kochka. Their task? Kill all the scarabs, an invasive alien species that is trying to turn Earth into their new home. Or is that all that's behind it?

In the slums of paradise only the wicked survive

Senna isn't the strongest, the fastest, or even the smartest Blade and she's painfully aware of it, all while tangling with her unrequieted crush on one of her fellow Blades.

When the world dies, the parade begins

Juggle Senna's everyday life and her fight against the scarabs under her secret identity of 02-Ember Scarlet. 

Bring her to victory.

Or to question herself about the reality of her situation.

Find your way

Mors Blade features:

  • 80'000 words split into four paths

  • three endings plus a golden route accessible after completing all of them

  • hand-crafted cutscenes and stills, drawn on paper, inked, scanned, and then digitally colored

  • a marketable (?) rabbit robot

  • a certain yellow-hatted bartender that is totally not related with another yellow-hatted bartender

  • violent fights against alien creatures

  • romance between three dorks, in different combinations

UNSLASHED!

The Steam version of Mors Blade comes with an in-game gallery, achievements, cloud saves, and some extra content

content_details.name: Lost Emblem of Time
content_details.short_description: A retro 8-bit JRPG just like the classic final fantasy games. You know with turn-based combat and a story-driven adventure. Explore a vast world filled with dangerous enemies, mini-games, ect.
content_details.about_the_game:
Do you ever feel that newer final fantasy games doesn't feel the same like in the past? Do you ever want to go back in a new experience? Well, this game is for you! 

A retro 8-bit-style JRPG featuring turn-based combat and a deeply story-driven adventure. Journey through a retro and expanding world filled with dangerous enemies, engaging mini-games, hidden treasures, and a wide variety of locations to explore. As you progress, uncover secrets, grow stronger, and experience an emotional narrative that continues to expand with every step of your journey.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Long ago, in a world of fantasy, a powerful force of darkness began to rise. A ruthless ruler seized the Crystal of Darkness, gaining unimaginable power and forming his own army, the Imperials. With this strength, he seeks to plunge the world into ruin by unleashing the Fog of Darkness, a force capable of consuming everything in its path.

The ancient Heroes of Light once stood against him, however, they never make it. 

Now, with the world on the brink of collapse, the light calls out once more: choosing four new heroes to take their place.

Emily, Lancer, Leon, and Rem are drawn together by fate, though each of them is burdened by their own struggles and past. Reluctant or not, they must rise to face a destiny far greater than themselves.

To stand against the Dark Lord and his Imperials, they must seek out the four sacred crystals: Earth, Flame, Water, and Light. Before darkness claims them first.

The fate of the world now rests in their hands.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Short disclaimer: This game is work of fiction. 

The art is from RPG Maker MV DLC pack, but I edited some of the art, using the same style (No ai of course). The music as well...

Although, some music may be copyrighted as the following one: Final Fantasy IV: Dancing Calcobrina but in 8-bit. 

made by Jilly Shears 

It will be removed (including the whole game) if Square Enix ask/tell me to do so. 

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

content_details.name: Neon Hustle
content_details.short_description: A first-person management sim set in a living crime-noir town. Recruit workers, pitch clients on the street yourself, manage rising city heat, and keep the operation running before the night forces itself to end. Mature themes, no explicit content.
content_details.about_the_game:
A first-person management sim where you run a street-level operation in a crime-noir border town — recruit, place, price, and protect, from dusk until the day forces itself to end.

You're not clicking through menus from a distance. You're walking the streets yourself — pitching passersby, hauling supplies, flipping motel rooms, and throwing punches when things go wrong. Every system in this game is something you can put your hands on.

Run the operation
Recruit workers, negotiate terms, and station them around town. Set prices, manage a roster with real stats and real limits, and watch your choices show up in the ledger the next morning.

Work the streets yourself
Approach pedestrians directly and pitch them — read the situation, offer a discount, or make your case with confidence. A deal you close yourself always pays better than one that happens without you.

Manage real risk
The city has its own heat — push too hard in one part of town and the consequences follow you there specifically. Robberies, harassment, and undercover cops are all real threats you have to notice and respond to in real time, on foot, before it's too late.

A town that runs without you
Pedestrians go about their own schedules. A courier keeps his own hours. Danger rises and falls with the time of night. You're one operator in a town that keeps moving whether you're watching or not.

Keep the lights on
Wages, rent on your rooms, upkeep, bail — nothing is free, and nothing waits for you to catch up. Every night ends whether you're ready or not, and the next one starts a little riskier than the last.

First-person management sim set in a living, systemic crime-noir town

  • Recruit, negotiate, and manage a roster with real, evolving stats

  • Hands-on street pitching — approach pedestrians and close deals yourself

  • Zone-based City Heat system — risk that responds to where you operate, not just how

  • Real-time threats: robbery, harassment, and undercover police

  • Physical motel management — turn over rooms, restock supplies, clear it for the next session

  • A day/night cycle with a hard nightly cutoff — every night ends, ready or not

  • A courier, pedestrian traffic, and danger levels that all run on their own independent schedules

content_details.name: Voidshift
content_details.short_description: A psychological horror game about working the night shift in a store that reacts to your mistakes. Follow procedure. Avoid irregularities.
content_details.about_the_game:
You've got the graveyard shift at Edenway Market. Congratulations on your dead end job.

It's a quiet store. Not much to do, all things considered. Stock the empty shelves, mop the floors, clean the dirty bathrooms, check the coolers…just keep the place looking decent 'till morning. It's what you were hired to do, after all.

You're the only person working in this miserable excuse of a grocery store during the graveyard shift, and little mistakes have a way of becoming bigger problems…but don't worry about it. Just finish your work.

Clock in with Voidshift, a first-person psychological horror game in the summer of a vintage 1998. If you want to keep your job, completing all of your tasks before the end of the shift isn't the end of your worries. Something poisons the store, becoming more potent with each shift. It watches your every move, and with every mistake, it promises consequences.

The manager has made it clear that she will not hold your hand with any "mandatory training" nonsense; the only clear motion of objective is the task list in the break room. Despite this, you're expected to complete your nightly tasks in an inconsistent environment while pressure builds as you are haunted by threats you cannot describe. You feel like you are constantly being watched…but you refuse to let your paranoia take away your paycheck.

Whatever you do?

Don't make the same mistake twice.
